Sastry et al. — Computing Power and the Governance of Artificial Intelligence (2024)

Sastry, Heim, Belfield and co-authors argue that computing power is an unusually effective point of intervention for AI governance, because compute is detectable, excludable, quantifiable and produced through an extremely concentrated supply chain. They set out how compute could enhance three governance capacities — visibility, allocation and enforcement — while cataloguing its limits and the risks of naive approaches, and proposing guardrails. The Oggy Assessment presses on compute as a proxy for risk and on what compute governance can and cannot do for real-time oversight of deployed AI.
